name: awesome-decentralized-web
desc: A curated list of peer-to-peer, federated, and local-first protocols, applications, and developer tools. Excludes cryptocurrency, tokens, and AI agents.

resources.name: ActivityPub
resources.desc: W3C Recommendation (2018) for federated social networking, defining server-to-server and client-to-server APIs; the protocol behind most of the Fediverse.

resources.name: AT Protocol
resources.desc: The Authenticated Transfer Protocol, an open protocol for decentralized social networking with portable identities (DIDs), powering Bluesky; global views of the network rely on resource-intensive Relay and AppView services.

resources.name: ForgeFed
resources.desc: ActivityPub extension for federating software forges: a server-to-server API for pull requests, forks, and subscriptions; implemented experimentally by Forgejo.

resources.name: Matrix
resources.desc: Open specification for federated, persistent communication rooms whose history is replicated across every participating homeserver rather than owned by one; bridges connect it to other chat networks.

resources.name: Nostr
resources.desc: Minimal protocol in which cryptographically signed notes are published to any number of independent relays; identity is a client-side keypair, and removing content requires every relay carrying it to cooperate.

resources.name: Scuttlebutt
resources.desc: Offline-first gossip protocol that replicates signed append-only feeds between mutual follows over LAN or internet; no servers are required, though optional pub and room servers aid discovery.

resources.name: XMPP
resources.desc: The Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol, an open IETF standard for federated messaging with thousands of independently operated servers.

resources.name: BitTorrent
resources.desc: The dominant peer-to-peer file-distribution protocol, specified as open BEPs; swarms find each other through trackers or the Mainline DHT.

resources.name: cjdns
resources.desc: Encrypted IPv6 overlay network with distributed hash table routing.

resources.name: GNUnet
resources.desc: A network protocol stack for building secure, distributed, and privacy-preserving applications, with strong roots in academic research.

resources.name: Hypercore Protocol
resources.desc: A fast, scalable, and secure peer-to-peer protocol for everyone (evolution of the Dat Protocol), now maintained by Holepunch as part of the Pear runtime.

resources.name: IPFS
resources.desc: The InterPlanetary File System, a content-addressed, peer-to-peer protocol for storing and sharing data; content stays retrievable only while some node pins it, and default nodes bootstrap through project-run infrastructure.

resources.name: IPLD
resources.desc: A content-addressed linked-data model underlying IPFS and related systems.

resources.name: Iroh
resources.desc: A toolkit for direct peer-to-peer connectivity: QUIC hole-punching, content-addressed blobs and document sync.

resources.name: libp2p
resources.desc: A modular peer-to-peer networking stack, the connectivity layer used by IPFS and many other decentralized projects.

resources.name: Named Data Networking
resources.desc: A content-centric Internet architecture with active research implementations such as NFD.

resources.name: WebRTC
resources.desc: W3C Recommendation (2021, with companion IETF RFCs) for direct browser-to-browser media and data channels; peers still need an application-provided signaling channel and commonly STUN/TURN servers to establish connections.

resources.name: Yggdrasil
resources.desc: An end-to-end encrypted IPv6 overlay network that scales without central coordination.

resources.name: Fedify
resources.desc: A TypeScript framework for building federated server applications on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Freenet
resources.desc: A decentralized, real-time platform for building and running applications entirely on a peer-to-peer network; a ground-up rewrite by the original Freenet founder (the classic Freenet lives on as Hyphanet).

resources.name: Holochain
resources.desc: A peer-to-peer protocol for data sharing and integrity, backed by authoritative hashchains for data provenance.

resources.name: Pear
resources.desc: A peer-to-peer application runtime and deployment system built on Hypercore, by Holepunch.

resources.name: Spritely
resources.desc: Distributed object-capability framework (Goblins, OCapN) for building the decentralized social web.

resources.name: Veilid
resources.desc: An open-source, peer-to-peer, mobile-first networked application framework with strong privacy, by Cult of the Dead Cow.

resources.name: WebXDC
resources.desc: A specification for portable web apps that run inside chat messages and sync over any transport, with no server of their own.

resources.name: Automerge
resources.desc: A CRDT library for building local-first, collaborative applications that sync without a central server.

resources.name: Earthstar
resources.desc: An offline-first, distributed, syncable, embedded document database for use in peer-to-peer software.

resources.name: m-ld
resources.desc: Library enabling consistent, zero latency read and write of shared information, using RDF (JSON-LD) and CRDTs. Dormant (no repository activity since 2024-08)

resources.name: p2panda
resources.desc: A collection of building blocks for local-first, peer-to-peer applications.

resources.name: Willow
resources.desc: A protocol for synchronisable, multi-writer data stores, by the authors of Earthstar.

resources.name: Yjs
resources.desc: A high-performance CRDT for building collaborative, offline-first applications.

resources.name: LibreMesh
resources.desc: A modular framework for creating OpenWrt/LEDE-based firmwares for wireless mesh nodes.

resources.name: Meshtastic
resources.desc: Open-source, off-grid mesh communication over inexpensive LoRa radios; channel encryption defaults to a well-known shared key, with private channels and public-key direct messages available.

resources.name: Reticulum
resources.desc: Cryptography-based networking stack for building resilient networks over almost any medium: LoRa, packet radio, WiFi or TCP/IP. Released under a custom non-OSI license with field-of-use restrictions.

resources.name: Decentralized Identifiers
resources.desc: W3C standard for globally unique, cryptographically verifiable identifiers that need no central registry.

resources.name: Decentralized Web Nodes
resources.desc: DIF draft specification for personal datastores that sync between a user's own nodes with built-in permissions. Dormant (no repository activity since 2024-09)

resources.name: Encrypted Data Vaults
resources.desc: A privacy-respecting mechanism for storing, indexing, and retrieving encrypted data at a storage provider.

resources.name: remoteStorage
resources.desc: An open protocol for decoupling data from apps.

resources.name: Solid
resources.desc: Specification for personal data pods with app-agnostic access control, based on Linked Data principles; the published protocol is at version 0.10, but real-world deployment remains small.

resources.name: Akkoma
resources.desc: Fork of Pleroma, a lightweight federated social networking server on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Bluesky
resources.desc: Social network built on the AT Protocol; personal data servers are self-hostable, but in practice the network depends on resource-intensive Relay and AppView services that few parties other than Bluesky operate.

resources.name: Bonfire
resources.desc: Modular open-source framework and application for building federated digital spaces.

resources.name: BookWyrm
resources.desc: Federated social reading and book reviews, on ActivityPub.

resources.name: diaspora*
resources.desc: Federated social network with its own protocol, organized around aspects (contact groups); one of the oldest running Fediverse projects (2010).

resources.name: Friendica
resources.desc: Federated social platform that speaks several protocols at once — ActivityPub, diaspora*, and others — acting as a bridge between networks.

resources.name: GoToSocial
resources.desc: Lightweight ActivityPub social network server.

resources.name: Hubzilla
resources.desc: Federated publishing and social platform built on the Zot protocol, whose nomadic identity lets an account and its data move or mirror between servers.

resources.name: Lemmy
resources.desc: Federated link aggregator and discussion forum, on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Manyverse
resources.desc: Mobile client for Secure Scuttlebutt, an offline-first gossip protocol that syncs social feeds over LAN or internet; content can be encrypted, but the social graph and metadata are public by design.

resources.name: Mastodon
resources.desc: Decentralized, federated alternative to Twitter.

resources.name: Mbin
resources.desc: Federated content aggregator and microblogging platform (community fork of /kbin), on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Misskey
resources.desc: Feature-rich federated microblogging platform on ActivityPub (Sharkey is a popular fork).

resources.name: Mobilizon
resources.desc: A federated tool that helps you find, create and organise events.

resources.name: PieFed
resources.desc: Federated link aggregator and discussion forum with a focus on moderation tooling, on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Pixelfed
resources.desc: Federated photo sharing, on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Pleroma
resources.desc: A federated social networking platform.

resources.name: Socialhome
resources.desc: Decentralized and federated profile builder with social networking features.

resources.name: Castopod
resources.desc: Self-hosted podcast hosting with ActivityPub federation.

resources.name: Funkwhale
resources.desc: A community-driven project that lets you listen and share music and audio within a decentralized, open network.

resources.name: Mediagoblin
resources.desc: A free software media publishing platform alternative to Flickr, YouTube, SoundCloud.

resources.name: Owncast
resources.desc: Self-hosted live video streaming with ActivityPub federation.

resources.name: PeerTube
resources.desc: Decentralized federated video streaming platform using P2P, ActivityPub and WebTorrent.

resources.name: WriteFreely
resources.desc: Minimalist federated blogging platform, on ActivityPub.

resources.name: Berty
resources.desc: Peer-to-peer messenger over libp2p with Bluetooth LE and local-network proximity transports, requiring no accounts or servers; still beta software.

resources.name: BitMessage
resources.desc: Encrypted message broadcasting in which every node relays every message, hiding who reads what; the network still runs, but the reference client's last release was in 2018.

resources.name: Briar
resources.desc: Messenger that syncs over Tor when the internet works and over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi when it does not; relays only between mutual contacts, not strangers. Audited by Cure53 (2017).

resources.name: Cwtch
resources.desc: Metadata-resistant group messenger built on Tor onion services, with untrusted relay servers for offline delivery.

resources.name: Delta Chat
resources.desc: Decentralized messenger with end-to-end encryption that works over the existing e-mail network.

resources.name: Jami
resources.desc: Distributed peer-to-peer communication (text, voice and video), free and open-source.

resources.name: Retroshare
resources.desc: Establish encrypted connections between you and your friends to create a network of computers, and provides various distributed services: forums, channels, chat, mail.

resources.name: Ricochet Refresh
resources.desc: Maintained fork of Ricochet in which every user is a Tor onion service, leaving no server-side metadata; the original was audited by NCC Group (2016), before the v3 onion migration.

resources.name: SimpleX Chat
resources.desc: Private messenger without any user identifiers, using decentralized relay servers.

resources.name: Tox
resources.desc: Serverless peer-to-peer encrypted messaging protocol and implementations (its own documentation notes it has not been independently audited).

resources.name: Darcs
resources.desc: Free and open source cross-platform distributed version control system.

resources.name: Forgejo
resources.desc: Self-hosted software forge (Gitea fork) implementing ActivityPub-based federation via ForgeFed.

resources.name: Pijul
resources.desc: A free and open source (GPL2) distributed version control system.

resources.name: Radicle
resources.desc: Secure peer-to-peer code collaboration without intermediaries.

resources.name: instant.io
resources.desc: Streaming file transfer over WebTorrent, entirely in the browser with nothing to install.

resources.name: magic-wormhole
resources.desc: Transfers files between two computers using short one-time codes over a PAKE-encrypted connection; a public rendezvous server (self-hostable) assists the handshake.

resources.name: OnionShare
resources.desc: Hosts the selected files as a hidden service on the user's computer.

resources.name: Peergos
resources.desc: End-to-end encrypted, peer-to-peer file storage, sharing and communication network.

resources.name: Perkeep
resources.desc: Personal, content-addressed storage system designed for lifelong data archiving independent of any provider; development continues at a slow pace.

resources.name: Syncthing
resources.desc: Continuous peer-to-peer file synchronization that works fully on a LAN with no internet; relay and discovery servers are optional and self-hostable.

resources.name: Tahoe-LAFS
resources.desc: A private, encrypted file storage system that decentralizes data across multiple servers.

resources.name: Tribler
resources.desc: Privacy enhanced BitTorrent client with P2P content discovery.

resources.name: WebTorrent
resources.desc: An in-browser torrenting that works without requiring users to install anything extra.

resources.name: GUN
resources.desc: Real-time graph database that syncs between JavaScript peers, in practice through relay "super peers"; conflict resolution is eventually consistent, with optional encryption via its SEA module.

resources.name: OrbitDB
resources.desc: Peer-to-peer database engine of append-only, CRDT-merged logs replicated over IPFS pubsub; eventually consistent, with availability depending on which peers are online.

resources.name: Hidden Lake
resources.desc: Anonymous friend-to-friend network built on queue-based messaging, designed to resist traffic analysis even by a global observer.

resources.name: Hyphanet
resources.desc: Formerly Freenet, a network aimed at activists and people living in repressive regimes (the new Freenet is a separate rewrite by the same founder). It uses a web of trust in high security mode, which makes users on the network very difficult to detect.

resources.name: I2P
resources.desc: Decentralized garlic-routing overlay for hidden services and peer-to-peer applications; recent academic work documents design weaknesses across its implementations.

resources.name: Tor
resources.desc: Onion-routing anonymity network, the base for onion services and the pluggable-transport ecosystem; repeatedly audited (most recently Cure53, 2023) with a publicly tracked vulnerability history.

resources.name: Agregore
resources.desc: A minimal web browser for the distributed web. Supports IPFS, Hypercore Protocol + more.

resources.name: Cactus Comments
resources.desc: A federated comment system for the open web built on Matrix.

resources.name: Ceno Browser
resources.desc: Censorship-resistant mobile browser that shares and retrieves web content through the Ouinet peer-to-peer cache.

resources.name: IPWB
resources.desc: An interplanetary wayback machine.

resources.name: yacy
resources.desc: Distributed Peer-to-Peer Web Search Engine and Intranet Search Appliance.

resources.name: Dark Crystal
resources.desc: Set of protocols, libraries, techniques and guidelines for secure management of sensitive data such as cryptographic keys.

resources.name: Keyoxide
resources.desc: Decentralized, cryptographic identity proofs; a self-hostable Keybase alternative.

resources.name: OpenTimestamps
resources.desc: A standard format for blockchain timestamping.

resources.name: AvionDB
resources.desc: Mongodb-like database on top of OrbitDB. Discontinued

resources.name: Backfeed
resources.desc: A technology to enable decentralized and user-owned governance and reputation management for a community. Discontinued

resources.name: Beaker
resources.desc: A peer-to-peer Web browser, made for users to run applications independently of hosts. Discontinued

resources.name: BigchainDB
resources.desc: A scalable database that layers blockchain technology over decentralized data. Discontinued

resources.name: Bit451
resources.desc: Decentralized / distributed anonymous peer-to-peer media network. YouTube meets BitTorrent meets Bitcoin. Discontinued

resources.name: bitnation
resources.desc: The World's First Virtual Nation – a Blockchain Jurisdiction. Discontinued (domain no longer controlled by the project; link goes to an archived copy).

resources.name: CacheP2P
resources.desc: A distributed caching platform. Discontinued

resources.name: Cryptosphere
resources.desc: An open-source P2P web application platform for decentralized, privacy-preserving software. Discontinued

resources.name: Dat Base
resources.desc: Future-friendly apps for your research data pipeline. Discontinued (the Dat project wound down).

resources.name: Dat Medium
resources.desc: A markdown blog system for Beaker inspired by Medium. Discontinued

resources.name: disaster.radio
resources.desc: A disaster-resilient communications network powered by the sun. Discontinued

resources.name: ferment
resources.desc: Peer-to-peer audio publishing and streaming application. Discontinued (repository deleted).

resources.name: git-ssb
resources.desc: Decentralized Git repo hosting and issue tracking on secure-scuttlebutt. Discontinued (repository archived in 2018).

resources.name: IPDB
resources.desc: A federated database network built on BigchainDB and IPFS. It is maintained by a network of caretakers around the world, at least half of which are nonprofits. Discontinued (site offline; link goes to an archived copy).

resources.name: Jolocom
resources.desc: A decentralised digital identity for everyone. Discontinued (domain squatted; link goes to an archived copy).

resources.name: LevelNews
resources.desc: A leftist news aggregator designed for an open web, and dedicated to journalism without censorship. Discontinued

resources.name: libdweb
resources.desc: A community effort to implement experimental APIs enabling dweb protocols in Firefox. Discontinued

resources.name: Mediachain
resources.desc: A media library built on IPFS that makes it easy to publish, track, and discover creative work. Discontinued (acquired by Spotify in 2017).

resources.name: Onename
resources.desc: Domain registrar for Blockstack. Discontinued

resources.name: OpenBazaar
resources.desc: Marketplace, with store fronts and moderators. Discontinued (shut down in 2021).

resources.name: ORC
resources.desc: The Onion Router Cloud, a distributed, anonymous, object storage platform owned and operated by all of us. Discontinued

resources.name: Patchwork
resources.desc: A decentralized messaging and sharing app built on top of Secure Scuttlebutt. Discontinued (repository archived; successor: Manyverse).

resources.name: PeerPad
resources.desc: A realtime P2P collaborative editing tool, powered by IPFS and CRDTs. Discontinued (site offline; link goes to the source repository).

resources.name: Ricochet
resources.desc: Completely anonymous and potentially metadata-free chat. Discontinued (domain squatted; link goes to the source repository).

resources.name: Rotonde
resources.desc: Decentralized social network defined as a shared JSON specification, whose clients ran over the Dat protocol; it faded when the Dat ecosystem wound down. Discontinued

resources.name: Samizdat
resources.desc: A platform for the self-hosted, peer-to-peer, cryptographically-secured internet. Discontinued

resources.name: Shift
resources.desc: Decentralized hosting infrastructure for dApps. Discontinued

resources.name: StrongLink
resources.desc: A searchable, syncable, content-addressable notetaking system Discontinued

resources.name: Swarm
resources.desc: A distributed storage platform and content distribution service of the Ethereum stack; the original Go implementation was archived, but the project remains active through the Bee implementation. Excluded (modern Swarm depends on BZZ token economics, out of scope for this list; kept here for the historical record).

resources.name: Tahrir
resources.desc: Encrypted, decentralized Twitter-style microblogging built on a web of trust, by Freenet's founder. Discontinued

resources.name: trsst
resources.desc: Encrypted, decentralized Twitter-style microblogging built on syndicated feeds. Discontinued

resources.name: Twister
resources.desc: A fully decentralized P2P microblogging platform leveraging the free software implementations of Bitcoin and BitTorrent protocols. Discontinued

resources.name: Webnative
resources.desc: JavaScript library that decouples user data from apps and hosts it on IPFS. Discontinued (Fission shut down in 2024).

resources.name: Wikipediap2p
resources.desc: A peer-to-peer version of Wikipedia. Discontinued

resources.name: ZeroNet
resources.desc: A peer-to-peer web built on the Bitcoin cryptography for addressing, and identity and Namecoin for .bit domains. Discontinued (site offline; community fork: zeronet-conservancy).

resources.name: alternative-internet
resources.desc: A collection of interesting new networks and technologies aiming at decentralisation.

resources.name: Awesome-decentralized-id
resources.desc: Resources for creating a Decentralized, Vendor Agnostic, Self Sovereign Identity System for people organizations and things.

resources.name: awesome-offline-knowledge
resources.desc: Content, tools, and infrastructure for keeping knowledge accessible without the internet.

resources.name: awesome-resilient-communication
resources.desc: A curated list of open protocols, applications, hardware, and resources for communication during internet shutdowns, disasters, censorship, and off-grid operation.

resources.name: delightful-fediverse-apps
resources.desc: A curated list of Fediverse applications and services.
